title: I made a full high quality voice pack for the old RPG "Tyranny". 46,000 lines spoken.
author: thewholeshelf
selftext:
I love the game Tyranny, but I always wished the whole of it was voiced. The parts Obsidian did voice are great, and then you hit a wall of text, which I accepted in the first playthrough, but has always kept me from re-playing it.

So I spent the last three months voicing everything else, and I just finished a full playthrough with it, and it was wonderful.

The voices and the portraits are AI-generated. I cast every character by hand, directed the lines and fixed problems as I went through the game. It's not the same as real voice actors, and it doesn't pretend to be. But if long text scenes wear you out, or you've always wanted the whole game voiced, I think it makes a real difference.

Here's a short video of it in game: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-cCd5XBGphg](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-cCd5XBGphg)

I did it using the elevenlabs API and a "voice studio" I custom made to help me go through each line and make sure it was as good as it could be.

Then I played the full game with various of the branches and corrected any take I found to sound wrong, and added "\[steering\]" when needed.

The total generation cost about **7.44 million elevenlabs credits** which is around **$1,230**. So it's not something I'm going to be repeating in the near future.

![img](5mdpxh6dsb3i1)

![img](430hjcgfsb3i1)

![img](b9jochthsb3i1)

  
**What the mod does:**

* Voices the dialogue the game left silent: companions, Archons, faction leaders, merchants, soldiers, townsfolk, barks. About 46,000 lines across roughly 800 speakers and 380 different unique voices (only very minor characters with under four lines are using the same voice actor).
* A narrator reads the descriptive text in conversations, plus the Conquest, edicts, inspections and scene intros.
* The expansion pack Bastard's Wound is included.
* Over 500 painted portraits for characters who only had the 3D paperdoll in conversations. One setting turns them off if you prefer the original look.
* Each companion and Archon keeps one voice the whole way through. If you'd rather hear the original actors on the lines they recorded, there's a setting for that too.

**Download (free):** [https://www.nexusmods.com/tyranny/mods/65](https://www.nexusmods.com/tyranny/mods/65)

comments.author: Defiant-Mood6717
comments.body:
$1,230 for 46k lines is about 2.7 cents a line, which is honestly less than I'd have guessed for hand-directed takes.

curious how you kept the companions consistent over three months. did you lock the settings per voice and only re-roll bad takes, or did you have to go back and redo early lines once you'd settled on how someone sounds? drift between takes made weeks apart is the part I'd expect to show up most on a full playthrough.

replies.author: thewholeshelf
replies.body:
With elevenlabs v4, there's not much drift honestly. I did have to change completely to a new character voice for some characters, even after having made hundreds and even thousands of lines, simply because they ended up not having the breadth of "voice acting". It turns out that many elevenlabs voices sounds fine in normal dialogue, but then can't yell or sound angry, which of course is a problem in a game like this.

The no-drift does come at a price where elevenlabsv4 "normalizes" many accents and make many voices sound more average. I hope to see them fix that in the future.
